newsitem.title: USA: GM to boost overseas capacity by 3 mln units.
newsitem.headline: GM to boost overseas capacity by 3 mln units.

text.p: General Motors Corp plans to increase its vehicle production capacity outside of North America to 5 million vehicles over the next 10 years from 2 million currently, analysts said Tuesday.

At a dinner meeting Monday night in New York, GM International Operations President Louis Hughes told analysts that the company would put 50 percent of the capacity expansion in place in 1997 and 1998.

In a research report, Smith Barney Inc analyst David Garrity said Hughes had revealed that GM's International Operations budgeted capital expenditures of $2.8 billion in 1997 and $2.8 billion in 1998, compared with $2.6 billion in 1996.

The capital expenditures, financed by the international operations' internal cash flow, should remain less than $3 billion a year during the expansion and will drop by $1 billion annually when it is completed, Garrity said.

The first part of the expansion includes nearly identical plants in Poland, Argentina, Brazil and Thailand. At these plants, GM will have flexible assembly capacity that will allow them each to produce two separate vehicle platforms and related variants.

"GM's (international operations) profit goal during the expansion period is to maintain the absolute level of profits through cost reductions realized through lower material costs, improved product quality and higher labor productivity," Garrity wrote.

In addition, Garrity said GM officials expected to earn better profit margins on the automaker's new Opel Astra platform cars, which will be launched in the fourth quarter of 1997 and the first quarter of 1998. The Astra, projected at 800,000 units annually, will benefit from delay in the launch of its major competitor, Volkswagen AG's next-generation Golf, which is now expected to enter the market at about the same time as the Astra, he said.
A GM spokesman was not immediately available to comment on the meeting with analysts.
